category_title: Young adults with intellectual disabilities who exhibit passive agreement and chronic lateness
minimal_context: Michael is in an IEP meeting with his teacher, job coach, mother, and program supervisor to discuss setting a goal for finishing tasks without stopping so much.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Michael, we would like to develop some goals with you. Your job coach says you have a tendency to pay more attention to what others are doing and can lose focus on what you need to be doing. Do you think that working on finishing tasks without stopping so much would be a good goal to work on?

STUDENT: Sure.

TUTOR: Your mom mentioned that you do the same thing at home, messing around in the morning instead of doing your job. So that is something that you could work on at both school and home.

STUDENT: Yeah, okay.

TUTOR: Do you think it is a problem, Michael?

STUDENT: I don't know. Maybe.

options.A: Expose the target behaviors to increased durations of access to reinforcement, providing one minute of access.
options.B: Simplify the goal-setting process by telling him, 'All you have to do is this, just do this part.'
options.C: Terminate the goal-setting demands and remove the meeting materials for 10 seconds during the discussion.
options.D: Do not accept 'maybe' or 'okay' as answers; instead, provide time and prompting during the discussion.
